decisions.costs: Renaming a Genres value means a fan-out update across every books document that carries it.
decisions.gains: Genres is a small, read-only lookup: duplicating (genre_name) into books documents removes the join from hot reads while the code field remains the join key for repairs.
decisions.mitigations: Lookups like this rarely change; when they do, batch-repair by the join key. The lookup collection can be dropped: nothing in the workload reads it alone.
decisions.subject: edge:Genres->books

decisions.costs: Reading a parent with its children needs a second query (or $lookup) instead of one document fetch.
decisions.gains: loans grows without bound (temporal column, no natural cap); keeping it separate avoids the 16 MB document ceiling and whole-document rewrites on every append.
decisions.mitigations: If recent-children reads matter, add a capped 'recent' array on the parent and treat it as a cache, not the system of record.
decisions.subject: edge:book_copies->loans

decisions.costs: The 0% of reads that want both need a second lookup or $lookup stage.
decisions.gains: 100% of book_copies access happens without books — an embedded copy would force $unwind on more than half the workload.
decisions.mitigations: If those joined reads are latency-critical, duplicate a small summary of the parent into the child (reads must dominate writes).

near_misses.detail: fan-out bounded at ~100 (capped column) — large but finite

decisions.subject: edge:books->book_copies

decisions.costs: book_details loses its own collection; anything that queried it standalone (currently 6%) must go through books.
decisions.gains: 1:1 via a unique foreign key and 57% co-access: two tables that are always read together become one document.
decisions.mitigations: Keep the child's unique key as an indexed field inside the parent document.

decisions.costs: Removing a authors from the vocabulary means updating every host document that carries it; the array index is multikey.
decisions.gains: authors is a bounded vocabulary: an array of ids + full_name on each books document answers the co-accessed reads in one fetch, one-way (no dual arrays to keep consistent).
decisions.mitigations: Vocabulary changes are rare; repair by scanning the array field when they happen.
